And my bow. But the big problem is we are heading towards socialized medicine, and obesity already costs us so much and it's only going to cost us (yes all of us) more. I don't hate people I hate fat. If you CHOOSE to be fat (yes it is a choice for everyone) then I will probably hate you. But I recognize when someone is a victim of improper upbringing.

On "improper upbringing," it's frightening seeing the handful of kids that are extremely overweight when I go to pick up my kids from school. They weigh twice as much as their classmates and it isn't remotely their fault. If there exists some medical issue that is compounding the problem, it absolutely must be addressed. If it is simply poor eating and exercising habits, it must be addressed. These are military brats, so they absolutely have access to healthcare.

This is arguably more of a problem of socialized medicine than of fat people. Before the licensing of physicians (creating an artificial monopoly within healthcare) and the rise of medicare, medicaid, etc., people paid for basic medical treatment out of pocket because it was as cheap as everything else. They also had a much more clear financial incentive to take care of their personal health since the costs of abusing one's body were not socialized across the entire system.

I'm not trying to derail the discussion and turn this into a debate about whether socialized medicine is good or not, but you have to admit that this and may other related issues (smoking, etc.) would be a lot easier to deal with at a certain level if everyone was responsible for their own healthcare.

As you can see I'm pretty neutral about the whole thing.

I hate any kind of excuses. I don't hate fat people, but I do hate it when people have a million excuses about why they can't do something. If you don't want to lose weight, that's fine, but don't complain constantly about being fat and then say, 'I can't lose weight because of [reasons].'

But for those people who genuinely think that mockery and hatred 'helps' someone, it usually doesn't. Especially not for someone who is struggling with the mental aspects of over-eating. It's hard to 'bully' someone into giving up a habit that they already know is bad and that they're already ashamed of. It tends to make a certain kind of person feel worse and retreat even further into the behaviour that's being mocked and, of course, seek out like-minded people to insulate themselves.

If you found out that one of your old friends was now addicted to heroin do you think that it would help him to tell him that he's a worthless junkie and to kill himself whenever you saw him? 9 times out of 10 all you'd accomplish was making him feel even more alienated from 'normal' people.

It's a really old-school type of style of 'helping', like telling returning soldiers to just 'be a man' and 'walk it off' instead of dealing with PTSD. For some people the fact that they're not able to just stop makes them feel even more worthless and wonder what the point is of even trying.

I think it's hard to solely blame fat people, when industry and incorrect diet advice plays such a big role.

People are misinformed about how to efficiently lose weight through diet and lower insulin resistance. The old just eat less do more exercise is one of the hardest ways to lose weight, especially when starting out from obese. This phrase gets repeated and it shows that the people saying it know as little as the person struggling with obesity. 90% of the problem is knowledge about diet and insulin. (insulin is important to understand even before you are diabetic)

Disclaimer: I'm a keto person, have been for over a year and a half and have lost loads of weight. This is from my keto perspective and what I have learned on my journey. You may disagree with the low carbs cult but if it helps someone here, like it has helped me then that's a massive bonus. I have lost the same amount of weight before through eating less and doing more exercise in the past but felt shit while doing it and found it hard to maintain. So I feel I can somewhat compare the two approaches. Also the science of keto is radically different from all other diets and quite hard for people to understand unless they have done some research into it. I do vilify the heavy carb diet, as an all year round diet, you have been warned.

Carb food cheap to produce thanks to subsidies, easy to store and versitile for making more complex products, therefore industries love them because they are profitable. This means that carbs are cheap to buy and readily available.

Carb heavy products out way other food groups in super markets 10:1, try shopping for keto you realise you can use 2 isles worth of food from a 20 isle supermarket. Almost all takeaways and fast food is very carb heavy, most medically suggested diets are carb heavy. Even diet foods are carb heavy and only labeled as diet because they contain no fat. (for example, one diet shake powder was 50% sugar and carbs but 0 fat)

This prevalence of a high carb lifestyle has ingrained itself on society, it has become normality. People think this is what a diet should look like, it is even being recommended here in the UK as the only way of controlling diabetes. When in reality eating too many carbs is increasing insulin resistance even further.

In a ketogenic state the body's main fuel source is fat, when hungry your body is literally eating your body fat. Your body in keto cannot store fat very well though and insulin levels remain homeostatic. Losing weight in this mode is actually effortless.

In a carb diet you are in a 'fat storage' mode riding an increasingly higher roller coaster of insulin, which means people trying to lose weight, on this approach, are rowing upstream, they need to be running at a large deficit to see substantial loss. Personally this made me fell like shit all the time.

Carbs and fat storing also makes sense from our ancestral seasonal eating habits (or at least mine from my research), Mainly carb foods are ready to be eaten at harvests time, to enable us to add weight on for the winter. These foods that were only available for a few months of the year are now available all the way throughout the year. People do not eat seasonally at all these days.

Insulin over-usage seems to be a large driving force in fatty liver and weight gain, it is more complex than most people think. Some people seem to be more reactive to insulin than others meaning they need less to gain the same response from the body.

Most people still think that you get diabetes because you're just fat, when actually massive weight gain is actually the bodies reaction to rising insulin resistance because the amount of carbs that have been processed until that point. So it kind of works in the opposite way to people's perceptions.

Many people have successfully reversed t2 diabetes through ketogenic or similar diets by reducing insulin resistance, it is the only natural cure and has been know about since the 1920s. Today doctors that know about this are massively in the minority. Doctors still learn that fat is bad and fruit is good but many have know for years that most fats aren't bad for you and sugars really are. Most fruits are much higher in sugar and lower in fibre than what our ancestors ate, also fruit juice is really bad for spiking insulin when the fibre is removed. Fruits are touted as being really healthy, when actually green veg is far more beneficial.

In my opinion if even doctors are giving incorrect advice then what hope does the average person really have.

For me it was luck, I stumbled across keto and as I started to understand how the body really works, based from modern science, not 1960s scare mongering and industry propaganda, the weight just started to fall off. I have gone from being obese to a bid podgy and it's been the easiest and tastiest lifestyle choice I have ever made. This is my path for life now, I will avoid diabetes, I hope many others can too.

So my point really is that people just don't have the knowledge that they really should to combat obesity. This includes doctors. People do have a personal responsibility of course, but many are sent on the wrong direction when they try to make things better. Hating fat people will just fuck with their self esteem which makes it harder to get started, giving people the tools and knowledge to take the best route is far more productive. We need to change society and the medical profession's views on diet as a priority before worrying about individual fat people.
